subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tran <sam.tran@atlaspayments.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Thanks for a productive call today — great to meet you all. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we have alignment before we kick off:

1) High-level goal
- Validate Redwood as a production-grade inference layer for Atlas Payments' Customer Support assistant (intent classification + response generation + reranking) with predictable latency, cost, and quality.

2) Success criteria / KPIs (what Atlas needs to validate)
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response latency < 200 ms (for 1-2 sentence replies) on production-like payloads.
- Throughput: sustain 500 concurrent sessions with median latency target < 120 ms; or baseline throughput of ~100k tokens/minute for batched workloads.
- Cost: average generation cost <= $0.0006 per token (target; include quantized model options).
- Quality: automated evaluation on Atlas test set — precision/recall F1 >= 0.85 for intent detection; top-1 response accuracy >= 90% on canned replies; overall hallucination rate < 2% on evaluation prompts.
- Reliability: no more than 1% error/timeout rate during a 72-hour soak test.

3) Evaluation plan
- Atlas provides a representative eval dataset (sampled customer inquiries + expected responses) and traffic profile (payload sizes, session concurrency, expected ramp).
- Redwood will run: baseline (current model config), 2 experiment configs (quantized + batching) and provide per-config metrics (latency histograms, cost per token, quality metrics).
- Tracking: shared dashboard (latency, token counts, cost, errors) + weekly scorecard.

4) Timeline (4-week trial)
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, credentials, dataset handoff.
- Week 1: infra provisioning + integration (SDK + test harness).
- Week 2: run baseline + initial experiments.
- Week 3: optimize batching/quant profiles and run soak.
- Week 4: final evaluation, scorecard, handoff and recommendation.

5) Ownership
- Atlas POC lead: Sam Tran (your side)
- Redwood: Jordan Blake (sales), Marissa Cole (CS lead, POC ops), Rishi Malhotra (solutions / infra tuning)

6) Next steps (action items)
- Atlas: share eval dataset and traffic profile by COB Tuesday (2026-10-22).
- Redwood: provision trial credentials + share PoC scope doc (attached) and trial runbook.
- Schedule 30-min kickoff once credentials are live — propose Wed 10/21 or Thu 10/22 (I’ll send calendar options).

Attachment: atlas_poc_scope.pdf — proposed test cases, data requirements, and the evaluation rubric.

If this looks right I’ll go ahead and provision the trial and schedule the kickoff.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Tran <sam.tran@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the 95th <200 ms target sounds good, but calling out that on first pass we expect some variance for longer context windows (we will provide typical context sizes).
- Throughput: 500 concurrent sessions is our upper bound — we'd like Alder to validate at week 3 that we can scale.
- Quality: when you say "top-1 response accuracy >= 90% on canned replies" — can you confirm whether that is measured on exact string match or semantic match? We can provide a labeled set and prefer semantic matching where applicable.

We’ll aim to get the eval dataset and traffic profile to you by Tuesday (10/22). Also tagging Andre Gomez (ops) on this thread to coordinate credentials and network allowlist.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah | Head of Product, Customer Experience
Atlas Payments
priya.shah@atlaspayments.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspayments.com>, Sam Tran <sam.tran@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments trial

Thanks Priya — great questions. Quick answers and updates:

- Measurement: for canned replies we’ll use semantic similarity + QnA grading (embedding cosine + human spot checks). We’ll include both exact-match and semantic-match columns in the scorecard so you can pick the one you prefer for decisioning.
- Latency variance: noted — we’ll include separate latency buckets by context length (short <128 tokens, medium 128-512, long >512).

Action updates:
- I’ve attached the PoC scope (atlas_poc_scope.pdf) and a short runbook (redwood_trial_instructions.txt) with steps for credentials, allowlist, and a test harness example.
- Marissa will lead day-to-day POC ops and Rishi will handle model/config tuning.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 10/22 10:30am PT — sending invite now.

Jordan
